description.ncbi_summary: Transducin is a 3-subunit guanine nucleotide-binding protein (G protein) which stimulates the coupling of rhodopsin and cGMP-phoshodiesterase during visual impulses. The transducin alpha subunits in rods and cones are encoded by separate genes. This gene encodes the alpha subunit in cones. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Alpha subunit of the heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide-binding protein (G protein) that transduces signals from the G protein-coupled cone photoreceptors (blue, green and red cones) (PubMed:12077706, PubMed:2534964). Functions as a GTPase, cycling between an active GTP-bound state and an inactive GDP-bound state. Upon photoactivation, cone photoreceptors promote GDP release and GTP binding (By similarity). In its active state, GNAT2 stimulates downstream effectors, including the cone cGMP-phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex, to mediate the phototransduction cascade (By similarity). Activation of the PDE6 complex occurs through binding and repositioning of the inhibitory PDE6 gamma subunits (PDE6H), thereby promoting catalytic activity (By similarity).
